The provided assertion requires grouping by stride (every nth element goes into the same sublist), not consecutive blocks. The team note describes consecutive blocks, which would give `[['a','b','c'], ['d','e','f'], ...]` and fail the assertion. I followed the assertion, since it is the concrete check the function must pass. The code is the same as the earlier answer; I checked by hand that it returns the expected output for the example.

```python
def list_split(lst, n):
    return [lst[i::n] for i in range(n)]
```
